The chain establishes the requested energy and target-independent operator for every smooth integral projective original X of positive dimension, every algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero k of arbitrary cardinality, and every actual big rational L. Nefness, finite generation, and a Zariski decomposition are unnecessary. This conclusion leaves original P16.5 open.

The external premises are indexed below. Passage −1 records the sole task grant and is deliberately excluded from the external-premise array. I use G0 only for genuine psh closure and divisorial determination inside an actual ample class; its ample energy, intersection mass, mixed products, and inverse theorem are never transferred to L.

1. General envelopes and the original reference. I opened the [BJ Addendum](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2206.07183v2), including Lemmas 1.3–1.7, the characteristic-zero proof of Theorem A, and Corollaries 2.1–2.2. In the needed big rational case, the multiplier-ideal approximants are already one actual defining net on L+A/m. Subadditivity and the shift making the auxiliary model function nonnegative give decrease in the divisibility order. A shifted nonzero section supplies a genuine minorant and prevents generic collapse. This membership step requires no abstract varying-class flattening. The reference and compactness inputs retain the smooth original domain and arbitrary cardinality. In particular V_L=P_L(0) is genuine, has generic value zero, and dominates every normalized genuine potential. For usc obstacles with a genuine minorant, envelope regularity and the obstacle inequality make the regularized supremum itself a competitor, so the envelope equals the unregularized supremum everywhere.

2. Algebraic inputs and their scope. I checked the pertinent positive-product construction, continuity, concavity, and differentiability units in [BFJ](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0608260v2). Every volume differential in the argument is applied on a smooth projective variety of dimension d=n+1, at a big Cartier class. The order comparisons concern Cartier classes and compatible Weil positive products. Their intersections with fixed pulled nef Cartier directions are legitimate nonnegative pairings; arbitrary nonnef central components are not used as order-preserving tests. Full section limits follow from the complete-series proof in [Lazarsfeld–Mustaţă](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/robert.lazarsfeld/Reprints/Laz.Mustata.CBALS.pdf), §§2.1–2.2. Its uncountable-field convention causes no restriction here: extending k to an uncountable algebraically closed field preserves each actual section space by flat base change, hence preserves the entire numerical sequence and its limit. Clearing a rational denominator gives the required divisible-degree limits. No finite-generation assumption enters.

3. Actual lattices, energy, and multiplicities. Proper direct image is coherent and torsion free over the smooth base curve, hence locally free. The fixed product trivialization and equivariance turn its lattice into a finite flag in R_m=H^0(X,mL). An adapted basis gives M_m=⊕_j k[t]t^(−w_m,j)s_m,j, with ma≤w_m,j≤mb. Gluing at infinity therefore gives the exact formula h^0(Y,mα_D(c))=∑_j max(w_m,j+mc+1,0). This is the all-c formula. The untruncated affine formula applies only once c>−a. Section asymptotics then give vol(α_D(c))=dcV+dE(D), where V=vol_X(L), and E(D)=lim_m n!m^(−d)∑_j w_m,j. Thus E(0)=0, constant shifts add sV, coefficientwise effective increments increase energy, and the sup-norm bound is V-Lipschitz. Expanding volume-root concavity at large c proves ordinary concavity of E, without asserting ordinary volume concavity.

For sufficiently large c, put q_i(D)=⟨α_D(c)^n⟩·E_i. Adding the effective E_i increases volume, so its derivative proves q_i(D)≥0. Differentiation in F=∑_i b_iE_i gives ∑_i b_iq_i(D)=V. A common eventual-affine half-line for D+tE_i proves independence of each q_i from c, rather than just independence of their sum. Consequently μ_D=∑_i b_iq_i(D)δ_(x_i) is positive and has raw mass V. Since f_H(x_i)=h_i/b_i, differentiation gives dE(D+tH)/dt|_0=∫f_H dμ_D, retaining every central multiplicity.

4. Birational invariance of both measures. For a refinement f:Y′→Y and effective exceptional G, normality gives f_*O_Y′(kG)=O_Y: permitted poles lie only above codimension at least two, and the height-one characterization of regularity excludes them downstairs. Projection formula therefore preserves sections and volume after adding nonnegative exceptional multiples to a pulled class. At a big class, differentiation makes every new exceptional coefficient zero. For a strict transform E_i′, the effective exceptional difference f^*E_i−E_i′ has zero pairing, so its coefficient equals the original coefficient. Strict transforms preserve b_i and x_i. This proves invariance of the full μ_D and, separately, of μ_D,c at every fixed c where α_D(c) is big. Common smooth equivariant snc refinements exist: close the common generic graph and apply functorial resolution to the central pair. The action and projection maps are smooth surjective, so functoriality supplies equivariance; resolution changes nothing away from the central fiber.

5. Section energy and genuine envelope-fiber descent. A single nonzero actual section gives a genuine generically finite FS function. Hence W_m(f;s)≥λ is equivalent, on the whole original carrier, to q_s+λ/m≤f and to q_s+λ/m≤P_L(f). For model obstacles, this is exactly the central regularity condition for st^(−λ). Horizontal divisors introduce no poles, and normality upgrades the prime-divisor test to regularity. Thus the genuine envelope determines every actual filtered coefficient space, in every divisible degree. Ordered envelopes order the flag weights without requiring a simultaneously adapted basis.

The flag-energy expression e_m(f)=n!m^(−d)∑_j floor W_m(f;s_m,j) consequently agrees with model energy and has the stated uniform comparison bound. Model density and the full section limit establish its limit E^obs(f) for every original continuous f. This functional is finite, concave, monotone, V-Lipschitz, translation equivariant, and ordered by genuine envelopes. In particular equal envelopes have equal energy.

Own144’s bounded-obstacle Taylor estimate is valid across all refinements. Its fixed big lower class gives the multiplicative class sandwich; positive-product order and homogeneity, paired separately with the two fixed nef summands of H, give the uniform derivative estimate. Positive fixed-mass measures then have unique weak clusters, determined by the two-sided derivatives against model functions and hence all original continuous functions. The minimum-obstacle argument descends these measures through equal genuine envelopes. The contact argument also checks out: continuous nonnegative tests supported inside a strict obstacle gap permit lowering the obstacle without changing its envelope, and Radon regularity exhausts that gap.

6. Entire genuine relative energy. The cone operations in own145 use actual defining nets. Tensoring with weight-zero generators changes the bundle while preserving the scalar function; common ample increments therefore produce genuine maxima. Increasing rational coefficients applied to nonpositive shifted stages produce real convex combinations. Every genuine potential embeds, as the same all-point function, in one fixed actual ample Ω. If finite FS stages are needed for the exact ample G0 convention, append the Ω generators at weight −k: max(φ_i,−k) is a single decreasing product-index net of finite FS functions. Continuous majorants, and then rational model majorants, have pointwise infimum u on every analytic point. Therefore E_L(u)=inf_(f continuous, f≥u) E^obs(f) is defined on the entire actual cone. It agrees with obstacle energy on P_L(f), satisfies E_L(V_L)=0 and E_L(u+c)=E_L(u)+cV, and never subtracts two infinite values.

For u_i↓u with genuine endpoint, the compact decreasing sets {u_i≥f+ε}, for a continuous majorant f of u, eventually become empty. This proves decreasing-net energy continuity, including energy −∞. Applied to u_k=max(u,V_L−k), it gives E_L(u)=inf_k E_L(u_k). After generic normalization, −kV≤E_L(u_k)≤0, so finite energy is exactly uniformly bounded relative-floor energy cost.

Concavity and the model derivatives give supporting planes A_D(u)=E^obs(f_D)+∫(u−f_D)dμ_D. Their atoms are divisorial or generic, and the actual-ample section-growth bound makes every coordinate finite. Passing continuous majorants down to u gives E_L(u)≤A_D(u); model majorants give the reverse infimum equality E_L(u)=inf_D A_D(u). Each plane is a finite continuous divisorial-coordinate sum. Energy is consequently weakly upper semicontinuous and concave, and normalized finite energy-cost sublevels are compact in the original weak topology.

7. Truncation and the coefficientwise tail. The all-c lattice formula, with its +1 error bounded by n!r_m/m^d→0, gives g_D(c)=lim_m n!m^(−d)∑_j(w_m,j+mc)_+. For D≤0 and E(D)≥−B, all weights are nonpositive. Thus g_D(0)=0, g_D is convex and V-Lipschitz, and cV−B≤g_D(c)≤cV. For c>B/V, α_D(c) is big. Volume monotonicity under each effective E_i proves positivity of μ_D,c, and differentiation in F gives its mass g_D′(c). Convexity gives V−B/c≤g_D′(c)≤V.

Effective lattice inclusion orders every actual flag weight, so T_(D+H)(c)≥T_D(c). Differentiating this monotonicity in E_i at a big α_D(c) gives q_i(D)−⟨α_D(c)^n⟩·E_i≥0. 8. Uniform margin and the full-energy derivative error. For α=α_D(c)≤γ with vol(α)≥κ=d(cV−B), follow α−rT until its first possible boundary point. Inside the big cone, positive-product order and the pulled nef T bound the volume loss by M=d⟨γ^n⟩·T. The integrated differential gives vol(α−rT)≥κ−Mr. Continuity at a boundary would force zero volume, contradicting this bound before r_0=κ/[2(M+1)]. Pairing the resulting positive-product bounds with fixed nef T_1,T_2, where H=T_1−T_2, proves a uniform fixed-c Taylor estimate. Normalize the original net by its convergent generic values and use the general θ compactness input to obtain a genuine θ cluster. Its divisorial coordinates coincide with the ample limit. All-point determination is then applied only to the two genuine Ω-potentials, establishing θ membership of the actual limit.

For u in the intrinsic relative E1 class, nonpositive model majorants carry one uniform energy lower bound. For every model direction h, their perturbed envelopes decrease to a genuine limit. The limit lies below u+th, while every genuine minorant of u+th lies below each envelope, proving whole-carrier equality with P_L(u+th). The bounds by u±|t|||h||∞ keep its energy finite. Decreasing energy continuity therefore passes the uniform model error to this actual envelope energy.

Both quotient signs followed by c→∞ give the derivative. Every weak cluster has the same model-test integral; uniform density and fixed mass identify a unique positive Radon cluster on all original C0 tests. This defines M_L(u), of raw mass vol(L), independently of targets and majorant choices. Uniform approximation of the direction, with energy error at most V|t|||h−h_m||∞, extends the two-sided formula to every continuous h. Its limit order is energy gap→0, then t→0, then c→∞. To compare u=P_L(g) with the earlier obstacle operator, take decreasing uniform upper model approximations g_i of the single continuous g and model majorants f_j of u. The model minimum b_i,j=min(g_i,f_j) still majorizes u, and 0≤E(g_i)−E(b_i,j)≤E(g_i)−E(u)→0 uniformly in j. Thus the ordered estimate proves M_L(u)=μ_g. The extension is genuinely compatible with the prior section/volume measures.

The ordered estimate passes to genuine E1 pairs. Decreasing-net energy continuity then proves M_L(u_i)→M_L(u) weakly for every decreasing genuine net with E1 endpoint. A decreasing net with a genuine weak endpoint has that same all-point endpoint by ample closure and determination. Finally, if u_i→u divisorially and E_L(u_i)→E_L(u), genuine w_i=max(u_i,u) converge divisorially to u. Monotonicity and upper semicontinuity squeeze E_L(w_i) to E_L(u). Both ordered energy gaps vanish, proving weak-plus-energy operator continuity against every original continuous observable. No countable replacement is used.

For every pseudoeffective θ, V_θ=P_θ(0) is genuine θ-psh, has supremum and generic value zero, and the supremum-zero genuine θ-psh cone is compact in the divisorial topology. [BJ Addendum, Theorem A and Corollaries 2.1–2.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2206.07183v2).

For a projective variety Y of dimension d over an uncountable algebraically closed field and any big Cartier divisor A, the full section asymptotic is a limit: lim_(m→∞) d! h^0(Y,mA)/m^d=vol_Y(A), with volume initially defined by the limsup. [Lazarsfeld–Mustaţă, Proposition 2.1, Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 2.3](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/robert.lazarsfeld/Reprints/Laz.Mustata.CBALS.pdf).

For a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme Y over a field k, a quasi-coherent sheaf F, and a field extension K/k, the natural map H^0(Y,F)⊗_k K→H^0(Y_K,F_K) is an isomorphism. [Stacks, flat base change](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02KH).

For a smooth integral projective d-fold over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, divisor volume is continuous on N^1_R, vanishes outside the big cone, equals the top positive product on the big cone, and its dth root is concave there. [BFJ, Theorems 2.16, 3.1 and 3.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0608260v2).

For a smooth integral projective d-fold over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, volume is C1 on the big cone, with Dvol_α(H)=d⟨α^(d−1)⟩·H for every real Cartier direction H. [BFJ, Theorem A](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0608260v2).

Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, positive products of big Cartier classes on the Riemann–Zariski space of a projective variety are homogeneous, continuous, and increasing in each variable for the pseudoeffective Cartier order, and produce compatible pseudoeffective Weil classes. [BFJ, §§2.2–2.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0608260v2).

Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, the Riemann–Zariski pairing of a nef Cartier divisor with a pseudoeffective Weil curve class on a projective variety is nonnegative and compatible with birational pullback and pushforward. [BFJ, Remark 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0608260v2).

For projective X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, X^an is compact Hausdorff. Rational model functions form a lattice containing rational constants, are uniformly dense in C0(X^an), and identify with vertical rational Cartier divisors modulo pullback. On an integrally closed test configuration, f_D≥0 iff D≥0; at a central component E, f_D(v_E)=ord_E(D)/ord_E(t), with v_E divisorial or generic. [BJ, §§1.4 and 2.1–2.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4).

For a projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and an actual ample line bundle A, every divisorial valuation v has finite maximal section vanishing order T_A(v)=sup_(m,s≠0) m^(-1)v(s). [BJ, Proposition 1.28](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4).

Every reduced noetherian quasi-excellent Q-scheme Y with a nowhere dense closed subset Z admits a projective birational resolution with regular source, simple-normal-crossings inverse image of Z, isomorphic outside Z∪Y_sing, functorial for surjective regular morphisms of pairs. [Abramovich–Temkin, §2.2 and Theorem 2.2.10](https://msp.org/ant/2019/13-2/ant-v13-n2-p04-p.pdf).
Every Noetherian normal domain R equals the intersection of its height-one localizations R_p inside its fraction field. [Stacks, Lemma 10.157.6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/031T).
